analysis: Only documentation changes were supplied: changelog.d/ssd-restore-without-eval-lock.md (new) and docs/architecture/inference.md (date bump plus a new paragraph at head ~line 252). No executable source was provided, so none of the code changes were examined. The docs describe a provider-staged complete-checkpoint SSD import that creates its destinations "already available from host bytes" and never evals or fences them. As a result, SSD restore no longer waits on MLX's process-wide evalLock while another request prefills. The changelog also mentions an opt-in live regression test. The relevant threat model entry is T-041 (SSD prefix cache, TB-007, A-001). The doc change does not alter documented crypto posture, HMAC lookup tags, TTL, account scoping or the SEC-035 accepted risk. Open questions for a pass that has the code (CompleteCheckpointTransfer.swift and SSDPrefixCache staging): (1) whether the skipped eval/fence leaves destination buffers aliasing host Data longer than the reservation or staging release accounting allows (the endAdoption/completeStaging backstops in T-041's detection_hint); (2) whether decrypted plaintext KV host bytes are retained or zeroed; (3) whether faster contended staging changes the TTFT timing oracle, which stays within the accepted SEC-035 risk. Nothing in the supplied text indicates a security regression, and the lack of source is a coverage limit rather than evidence of safety.
